title: Escalation Step Counting on Workplace Cafe Management Program Contracts
content:
A contract held under the Workplace Cafe Management Program may open its term well before a counter first serves, and the day the cafe first served is recorded on the contract in its own right. Which of those two days the escalation steps are counted from, and whether any step is counted at all, is what this note settles.

### The rule

Where a first service day is recorded on the contract and it falls more than thirty calendar days after the first day of the contract term, the escalation steps are the whole years between the first service day and the day the invoice is raised; where a first service day is recorded and it falls thirty calendar days or less after the first day of the term, the escalation steps are the whole years between the first day of the term and the day the invoice is raised; and where no first service day is recorded, no escalation step is taken.

### The same rule as a judgement in three settings

1. A first service day is recorded, and the gap between the first day of the contract term and that first service day is more than 30 calendar days. The escalation steps are the whole years between the first service day and the day the invoice is raised.
2. A first service day is recorded, and that gap is 30 calendar days or less. The escalation steps are the whole years between the first day of the term and the day the invoice is raised.
3. No first service day is recorded on the contract. No escalation step is taken.

### Where the boundary falls

The gap is counted in calendar days, every day of the calendar counting, from the first day of the contract term to the first service day recorded on the contract. A gap of exactly 30 calendar days is a gap of 30 calendar days or less, and the counting anchor is then the first day of the term. Only a gap of 31 calendar days or more is more than 30 calendar days. Whole years are counted between the anchor day and the day the invoice is raised, so a year begun but not completed adds nothing.

### Dated illustrations, on hypothetical records

Take a hypothetical contract whose term first day is 2024-03-02 and on which the invoice is raised on 2026-03-15.

- Hypothetical first service day 2024-04-01: that is 30 calendar days after the first day of the term, so the steps are the whole years between 2024-03-02 and 2026-03-15, being 2.
- Hypothetical first service day 2024-04-02: that is 31 calendar days after the first day of the term, so the steps are the whole years between 2024-04-02 and 2026-03-15, being 1.
- No first service day recorded on the contract at all: no escalation step is taken.
